verdict.summary: Getting it working on your own store is quick: create the app in the Dev Dashboard, paste the Composio callback URL, and add client_id and client_secret to Composio. Serving unrelated merchants needs a public app, which requires Shopify App Store review plus protected-customer-data approval, and Shopify does not publish a review timeline.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 30-60 min for Gate 1 and 2 (own store or custom install); several days of listing and compliance work plus review wait for Gate 3
verdict.time_to_first_connection: About 30-60 min once you have a Partner organization and a development or custom-distribution store
verdict.approval_wait: No official figure. Third-party sources cite about 5-14 business days; forum posts describe 1-3 weeks. Not verified on a Shopify page.

gates.name: Own app, own account (development or custom install)
gates.unlocks: You create the app, add Composio's redirect URI, and connect your own Shopify store through Composio using your client_id and client_secret.
limits: The app must sit in a Partner organization, because the Distribution card only appears for those apps (f9).
The distribution choice cannot be changed later (f8).
The legacy Shopify-admin custom app type can no longer be created (f6, f31).
gates.time_to_reach: Under 1 hour once a Partner organization exists

gates.name: Invited merchants on custom distribution or development stores
gates.unlocks: Custom distribution: an install link for one store, or several stores inside one Plus organization. Unapproved public app: installs on development shops from your Partners account.
limits: Custom distribution cannot serve unrelated merchants (f16).
Unapproved public apps cannot be installed on production stores (f13, f47).
No install cap or user limit for unreviewed public apps is documented (f56).

Unlisted public distribution is contested. Official docs describe limited visibility (f10, f11, f12), but a developer reports the dashboard offers only Public or Custom (f14), and a community answer says unlisted public apps still need review (f15).
gates.time_to_reach: Same session as Gate 1 for custom; immediate for development shops

gates.name: Public App Store app (anyone can install)
gates.unlocks: Installation on any merchant store through the Shopify App Store, with a listing page, after review.
limits: App Store review and automated checks must pass before submission (f33, f34).
Protected customer data access cannot be requested while the app is under review (f38).
Repeated failed review exchanges or unanswered emails can trigger a cooldown, and later cooldowns are longer (f39).
Listed apps are periodically audited after launch (f54).
Expiring tokens apply to public apps (f29, f30; unconfirmed on a Shopify page).
gates.time_to_reach: Not officially documented; third-party estimates run from about 5 to 14 business days after submission, and forum reports run longer

steps.title: Confirm you have a Partner organization and can open the Dev Dashboard
steps.detail: Sign in at dev.shopify.com/dashboard with the account that owns or administers a Partner organization. The Distribution card, which you need in a later step, only appears for apps inside a Partner organization. The account prerequisites were not confirmed from a live page, so check them when you sign in.
gotchas: The probe got HTTP 406, so the page was not confirmed directly.
Apps created in a store's own organization get the Installs card instead of the Distribution card.

steps.title: Create the app in the Dev Dashboard
steps.detail: Create a new app in the Dev Dashboard. Do not use the legacy Shopify-admin custom app type, because new ones can no longer be created.
gotchas: Legacy custom apps cannot be created starting January 1, 2026 (community quote of Shopify docs).
Existing legacy apps keep working.

steps.title: Choose the distribution method on the app's Home page
steps.detail: On the app's Home page, choose Custom distribution if the app will only serve one store or stores in one Plus organization. Choose Public distribution only if you plan to submit to the App Store. The choice cannot be changed afterwards.

values.label: Custom distribution
values.value: one store, or multiple stores in one Plus organization; no Shopify approval

gotchas: Public apps cannot be installed on production stores until they are approved (f13).
Once chosen, the distribution method cannot be changed.

steps.title: Set the Redirect URI in the app configuration
steps.detail: Add the exact callback URL from your Composio auth config as an allowed redirection URL in the Dev Dashboard. The value must match exactly, including scheme, path and trailing slash.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: Shopify requires an exact match with a redirect URI set in the Dev Dashboard or in shopify.app.toml.
A mismatch makes the authorization fail before any token is issued.

steps.title: Copy client_id and client_secret into a Composio OAUTH2 auth config
steps.detail: Copy the Client ID and Client secret from the app's settings. In Composio, create an OAUTH2 auth config for the shopify toolkit, paste both values, and enter the per-shop endpoints. Composio has no managed Shopify app, so you must supply these yourself.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: The {subdomain} is the merchant's myshopify.com shop name, not your app name.
S2S_OAUTH2 is listed for Shopify but has no URLs, so do not use it for this setup.

steps.title: Trim the scope list before authorizing
steps.detail: Have an agent take Composio's default scope list and cut it to the resources your use case needs. Keep read_ and write_ scopes separate, since a write scope already grants read. Mark any scope that needs Shopify approval or protected customer data access before you request it.

values.label: Scope rule
values.value: Request write_X only if you need both read and write on X

gotchas: The default list includes read_customers and write_customers, which bring review questions.
Scopes such as read_apps, read_shopify_payments and read_payment_gateways need Shopify approval before you can declare them.
Customer-name, email, phone and address scopes are protected data and return null until approved.

steps.title: Run a test authorization on your own store
steps.detail: Install the custom app on your development or custom-distribution store through its install link. Then connect the shop in Composio and confirm the token exchange works. Data from non-development stores can be blocked until protected-data approval is granted.

values.label: Shop
values.value: your development or single custom-distribution store

gotchas: Unapproved public apps only install on development shops.
The API will not return protected customer data from non-development stores until approval (f21).

steps.title: Implement token refresh before the access token expires
steps.detail: Have an agent update the token handling so the app requests an expiring offline token, stores the refresh token and its expiry time, and refreshes the access token shortly before it expires. Test the refresh on your store.

values.label: Token type
values.value: expiring offline token with refresh token

gotchas: Expiring access tokens are short-lived (official).
A third-party writeup gives a 60-minute lifetime, which is not confirmed on a Shopify page.
A third-party writeup says public apps on non-expiring tokens must migrate before January 1, 2027. Not confirmed on a Shopify page.

steps.title: Set up custom installs for each additional store in the Plus organization
steps.detail: For a custom app, generate the install link from the Dev Dashboard and install it on each store you need. Stores must belong to the same Plus organization, or the app must be limited to one store.
gotchas: Custom distribution cannot serve unrelated merchants (f16).
No install cap is documented, so confirm limits with Shopify before depending on one.

steps.title: Decide whether to go public, and if so, pick the listing visibility
steps.detail: Decide whether the app must reach merchants outside your organization. If it must, switch to Public distribution and pick full or limited visibility. Limited visibility is contested: official docs allow installs by direct link, while a community report says the dashboard shows only Public or Custom.

values.label: Visibility options
values.value: fully visible or limited visibility (changeable later in the Partner Dashboard Distribution section)

gotchas: Only fully visible apps appear in App Store search (f11).
A community answer says unlisted public apps still go through full review (f15).

steps.title: Draft the listing and compliance materials
steps.detail: Have an agent draft the privacy policy, pricing text, feature description and test instructions. Prepare 3-6 desktop screenshots at 1600x900, a feature video, a demo store URL and a 1200x1200 app icon. Use Shopify App Pricing for paid plans.
gotchas: Reviewers need working test credentials that grant full access (f42).
Domain names and the API contact email must not contain the word Shopify (f36).
Apps must avoid APIs deprecated within 90 days (f43).
Keep Lighthouse performance loss under 10 points on home, product and collection pages (f45).

steps.title: Implement compliance and GDPR webhooks
steps.detail: Subscribe the app to customers/data_request, customers/redact and shop/redact. Verify each HMAC signature and make each handler actually perform its function, such as deleting or exporting data.
gotchas: Reviewers check that the handlers actually work, not only that they exist.
Public apps must subscribe to compliance webhooks (official).

steps.title: Request protected customer data access from the submission page
steps.detail: Select a distribution method first, then request protected customer data access. Request only the data scopes the app uses. Public apps go through a review that covers Level 1 and Level 2 access, including evidence of your data practices.
gotchas: The request cannot be made while the app is under review (f38).
Non-public apps are reportedly approved automatically (community thread, unverified).
Declaring a scope does not grant access to protected data (f20).

steps.title: Run the automated App Store checks and submit for review
steps.detail: Fill in the app URLs, compliance webhooks, app icon and API contact details. Run the automated checks on the App Store review page and fix every failure before submitting. Give an emergency email and phone number for critical technical issues.
gotchas: Incomplete or beta submissions can delay review or cause rejection (f33).
The app must authorize with OAuth immediately, and after a reinstall too (f40).
Redirecting to your own login page after OAuth can fail the install check (f55).

steps.title: Wait for review and respond to requests
steps.detail: Shopify reviews the submission and may send questions. Answer every email quickly, since repeated unanswered emails and failed exchanges can trigger a cooldown. After approval, Shopify can still audit the listed app for performance.
gotchas: Repeated cooldowns grow longer each time (f39).
No official review timeline was found.

requirements.item: Partner organization account for the Dev Dashboard
requirements.detail: Distribution options and the Distribution card appear only for apps in a Partner organization. Account prerequisites were not confirmed from a live page.
The redirect_uri must exactly match a URI set in the Dev Dashboard or shopify.app.toml, and the full URL must be added as an allowed redirection URL.
Store the refresh token and expiry, and refresh before expiry. Public apps on non-expiring tokens reportedly must migrate before January 1, 2027, which is not confirmed on a Shopify page.

requirements.item: Custom distribution limited to one store or one Plus organization
requirements.detail: Custom apps cannot serve unrelated merchants and need no Shopify approval.

requirements.item: Public app installed only on development shops until approved
requirements.detail: Before approval, a public app can be installed only on development shops from the Partners account (staff reply in community thread).
Required for the App Store listing.

requirements.item: Demo store URL, screenshots, feature video and accurate pricing
requirements.detail: 3-6 desktop screenshots at 1600x900, a feature video, and a pricing section. Use Shopify App Pricing for paid charges.
Must be subscribed, HMAC-verified and functional.

requirements.item: App icon 1200x1200 and API contact details
requirements.detail: Part of the App Store configuration step. Contact email must not contain Shopify.
Shopify needs it for critical technical issues.
Run in the App Store review page and fix failures before submitting.

requirements.item: Test credentials with full access for reviewers
requirements.detail: Needed because third-party platform logins must come with working test credentials.
Public apps need review for Level 1 and Level 2 access, with evidence of data practices. Cannot be requested during app review.
Apps using APIs deprecated within 90 days cannot be submitted.
Public apps must authorize with OAuth before any other step, including after an uninstall.

scopes.effect: Standard Admin API access. A write_ scope also grants read on that resource, so request write only when both are needed.

scopes.scope: read_apps, read_checkout_settings, read_customer_payment_methods, read_marketplace_orders, read_payment_gateways, read_shopify_payments
scopes.effect: Shopify must approve the app for each scope before you can declare it. Request approval by contacting Shopify Support with your app and reason.
Protected customer data. Declaring is allowed, but data stays null or is withheld from non-development stores until approved, and public apps go through review.
Not in the protected pixel list in the changelog, but customer-level scopes draw review questions. Confirm whether they count as protected before submitting. Remove them if unused.

blockers.symptom: Cannot create a new custom app of the legacy Shopify-admin type.
blockers.cause: Shopify no longer allows new legacy custom apps, starting January 1, 2026. Existing apps keep working.
blockers.fix: Create the app in the Dev Dashboard and choose Custom distribution for a single store, or Public distribution for multi-merchant use.

blockers.symptom: Public app will not install on a production merchant store.
blockers.cause: Before approval, a public app can only be installed on development shops from your Partners account.
blockers.fix: Test on a development store, or submit for App Store review to reach production stores.

blockers.symptom: Customer data fields come back empty or null, or API calls return no data from non-development stores.
blockers.cause: Protected customer data is withheld until the app is approved for it. Declaring a scope is not the same as approval.
blockers.fix: Request protected customer data access from the submission page after choosing a distribution method, and request only the scopes you use.

blockers.symptom: Custom app cannot be used for a second, unrelated merchant.
blockers.cause: Custom distribution is limited to one store or stores within one Plus organization.
blockers.fix: Use Public distribution and go through App Store review.

blockers.symptom: App rejected by the automated install check after OAuth.
blockers.cause: The app redirected to its own login page after the grant instead of the expected Shopify flow.
blockers.fix: Keep the OAuth flow direct: authorize immediately on install, then redirect into the app.

blockers.symptom: Access stops working after tokens expire.
blockers.cause: Expiring offline tokens are short-lived and must be refreshed. A third-party source says public apps on non-expiring tokens must migrate before January 1, 2027.
blockers.fix: Implement refresh-token handling now. Confirm the migration deadline and token lifetime on a Shopify page before relying on them.

blockers.symptom: Integration depending on Script Tags or Shopify Scripts stops running.
blockers.cause: Per a third-party guide, Shopify Scripts stopped executing on June 30, 2026.
blockers.fix: Confirm whether your use case depends on Scripts. If it does, move the logic to a supported app approach.

blockers.symptom: App submission delayed or rejected for incomplete work.
blockers.cause: Submissions with errors, beta versions, or incomplete setup can be delayed or not approved. Repeated failed exchanges can trigger a cooldown.
blockers.fix: Run and fix all automated checks, complete every listing and compliance item, and answer Shopify emails promptly.

composio.note: Composio has no managed OAuth app for Shopify, so you must register your own Shopify app in the Dev Dashboard and supply its client_id and client_secret to Composio's OAUTH2 auth config. Use https://{subdomain}.myshopify.com/admin/oauth/authorize and /admin/oauth/access_token. The default scope list is broad, so trim it before review. S2S_OAUTH2 has no URLs.

open_questions: Review turnaround is not on any Shopify-owned page. Third-party sources give 3-14 business days, and a forum post cites a 5-10 business day official figure that could not be verified.
Whether the Dev Dashboard offers an unlisted public option is contested. Official docs describe limited visibility; a community report says only Public or Custom appear.
No install cap or user limit for unreviewed public apps was found on a Shopify page.
The January 1, 2027 migration deadline for non-expiring offline tokens and the 60-minute token lifetime come from a third-party writeup and were not confirmed on a Shopify page.
The Dev Dashboard returned HTTP 406 to the probe, so account prerequisites (Partner org, admin role, paid plan, business verification) were not confirmed from a live page.
The Shopify admin authorize endpoint returned a verification interstitial, not an OAuth error, for an invalid client_id. Client validation behavior is unverified.
